rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should test foundational design choices. This configuration tests multimodal (RNA + image) with singleprofile, pca_n2000 (basic RNA encoding), and imagenet_vit_l (standard image encoder) using simple concat fusion. It isolates the core question of whether multimodal approaches outperform single-modality baselines, while keeping other factors minimal to assess the baseline impact of combining modalities.

The existing evidence shows config_001 (multimodal, singleprofile) achieves 0.535 accuracy. Testing config_013 (multimodal, multiprofile with same RNA/image encoders but avgpool aggregation) isolates the impact of profile setting while keeping encoders consistent. This clarifies whether multiprofile improves performance and whether aggregation matters, addressing key design choices without overcomplicating changes.

The existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion (config_013) achieve high validation accuracy (0.715). This experiment tests whether switching to weighted fusion (while keeping image encoder and aggregation consistent) improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It builds on the strong foundation of config_013 while exploring a key design choice with minimal other changes.

Existing evidence shows config_013 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) achieves high accuracy (0.715). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder with pca_n2000 (used in lower-performing configs) while keeping other parameters identical would degrade performance, isolating the RNA encoder's impact. This clarifies if scvi_n200 is critical for performance, balancing exploitation of config_013's success with exploration of key design choices.

The existing evidence shows that config_013 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, avgpool, concat) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.715). This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from concat to weighted (while keeping other parameters identical) could further improve performance. This isolates the effect of fusion strategy, a critical design choice, and builds on the strong foundation of config_013. It balances exploitation of a promising direction with exploration of a key component.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal, multiprofile models with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion (config_013) achieve the highest accuracy (0.715). This experiment tests changing the image encoder from imagenet_vit_l to resnet50 and fusion from concat to weighted while keeping RNA encoder (scvi_n200) and aggregation (avgpool) consistent. This isolates the impact of image encoder and fusion method, which are critical design choices with sparse evidence in the current history.

Existing evidence shows that config_013 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, vit_l, avgpool, concat) achieves the highest accuracy (0.715). This experiment tests whether switching aggregation from avgpool to transformer (while keeping RNA/image encoders and fusion unchanged) improves performance. This isolates the impact of aggregation method, a critical design choice with limited prior evidence, and builds on the strong foundation of config_013.

Existing evidence shows multimodal multiprofile models with transformer aggregation (e.g., config_047) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching fusion from concat to weighted (while keeping RNA/image encoders and aggregation method identical) improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It directly compares a critical design choice with minimal parameter changes, leveraging the strong prior evidence of transformer aggregation's value.

Existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (as in config_043) yield high performance. This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder (resnet50 vs. imagenet_vit_l) while keeping RNA encoder (scvi_n200) and aggregation/fusion consistent isolates the impact of image encoder choice. It balances exploitation of proven components with exploration of critical design decisions.

Existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_043) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether using pca_n2000 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder in a transformer-aggregated, weighted fusion setup can match or exceed these results, isolating the impact of encoder choices on performance.
